os-settings-abstractions.title: Settings abstractions
os-settings-abstractions.summary: The nine setting kinds with their parsing rules, the models an admin screen shows and saves, and the stable codes. Small enough for a UI project to reference without the settings engine.

gives.1: Share the same models and error codes between the server and a UI library without pulling in the store, cache or sources.
gives.2: Write your own kind by deriving from `SettingKind<T>` and registering it with `AddOSSettingKind` in OS.Settings.

kinds.title: Kinds and rules
kinds.summary: How a text becomes a typed value, and the rules that limit it.

1.title: Text to value
1.text: A kind turns what a person typed into normalized text and a typed value.

2.title: No exceptions
2.text: `TryNormalize` returns either normalized text or a stable error key.

3.title: Nine built-in kinds
3.text: text, integer, decimal, boolean, url, path, duration, choice and list.

1.title: Converting text
1.text:
A kind turns the text a person typed into a normalized text and a typed value.

`TryNormalize` trims the text and checks the length and the rules. It returns either the normalized text or a stable error key, never an exception. `Read` and `Write` convert between that text and the value.

2.title: Built-in kinds
2.text:
text is any text and may be empty. integer is a `long`. decimal is a `decimal`, always written with a dot. boolean is there too.

url is http or https without a user name. path is a site-relative path that starts with a slash and has no `..` in it. duration is a `TimeSpan`, written like `00:00:30` for thirty seconds.

choice is one of the allowed options. list is comma separated and repeated items are removed.

3.title: Rules
3.text: `SettingRules` holds the minimum and maximum, the maximum length and the allowed options.

type.ISettingKind: A kind without its value type: name, normalizing and reading as an object.
type.ISettingKind{T}: A kind that reads and writes a value of type T.
type.SettingKind{T}: The base class of the built-in kinds. Derive from it to write your own.
type.TextSettingKind: Any text, up to 4,000 characters. May be empty.
type.IntegerSettingKind: A whole number as `long`, optionally within a range.
type.DecimalSettingKind: A decimal number, written with a dot in every culture.
type.UrlSettingKind: An absolute http or https address without credentials.
type.PathSettingKind: A path on the site, starting with a slash.
type.DurationSettingKind: A time span in the form `00:00:30`. A bare number is refused.
type.ChoiceSettingKind: One of the options in the rules, matched without regard to letter case.
type.ListSettingKind: A comma separated list, up to 256 items, optionally limited to the allowed options.
type.SettingRules: Minimum, maximum, maximum length and allowed options of a setting.

ISettingKind.TryNormalize: Checks a text against the rules and returns the normalized text or an error key.
ISettingKind.ReadObject: Reads a normalized text as an object.

SettingKind{T}.Read: Reads a normalized text as T.
SettingKind{T}.Write: Writes a value as normalized text.
SettingKind{T}.TryParse: What a kind overrides to accept its own format.

SettingRules.Min: The smallest allowed value. For a duration it counts seconds, and for a list it counts items.
SettingRules.Options: The allowed options of a choice or a list.
SettingRules.InRange: True when a number is between Min and Max.

models.title: Models
models.summary: What an admin screen reads and what it sends back.

1.title: Menu list
1.text: `SettingSectionHead` lists a section in a menu.

2.title: Section and items
2.text: `SettingSectionModel` is one section with its items.

4.title: Secrets have no value
4.text: A secret item never has its value.

1.title: Reading a section
1.text:
`SettingSectionHead` lists a section in a menu. `SettingSectionModel` is one section with its `SettingItemModel` items.

Each item has its key, kind, access, rules, current value and default. Where the value comes from is given by `SettingOrigin`. The version to send back and whether the item can be edited are there too.

A secret item never has its value, only `HasSecret`.

2.title: Saving and access
2.text:
To save, send a `SettingSaveModel` with the section, the scope and a list of `SettingChange` entries. Each is a new value or a reset, together with the version that was read.

`SettingAccess` says whether a key is public, internal, secret or system.

type.SettingOrigin: Where a shown value comes from: Default, Inherited, Own or Environment.
type.SettingChange: One change in a save: a value or a reset, with the version it was read at.
type.SettingItemModel: One setting as the screen shows it.
type.SettingSaveModel: A save request: section, scope and changes.
type.SettingSectionHead: The short form of a section, for a menu.
type.SettingSectionModel: A whole section with its items.

codes.title: Codes and limits
codes.summary: Names and limits that never change, so a UI can translate them.

1.title: Limits
1.text: Key, app code, text and list lengths have fixed limits.

2.title: Fixed names
2.text: The nine kind names and the configuration section name are fixed.

3.title: Translation keys
3.text: Error codes are keys for translation, not texts for people.

1.title: Limits and names
1.text:
`SettingCodes` holds the limits: key length 128, app code length 24, text length 4,000 and list items 256. It also holds the separators and the name of the configuration section, `OSSettings`.

`SettingCodes.Kind` has the names of the nine kinds.

2.title: Error keys
2.text:
`SettingCodes.Error` has the error keys that results carry. `settings.errors.range` is for a number out of range. `settings.errors.conflict` is for a stale version and `settings.errors.forbidden` is for a missing permission.

They are keys for your localization, not texts for people.

type.SettingCodes: Limits, separators and the configuration section name.
type.SettingCodes.Kind: The names of the nine kinds.
type.SettingCodes.Error: The error keys used by results and field errors.
